public_rationale: Marcus said the cost of building AI data centers was rising fast. A Bernstein report from June 8, 2026, the day of the post, estimated that a gigawatt of AI data center capacity on Nvidia's newest chips cost 17% more than on the previous generation. Bernstein said the main reason was memory and storage, and it noted storage prices had risen about 115% a year through May 2026. A rise of that size counts as rapid on an ordinary reading. Other industry data shows AI-driven increases in construction costs. The Stargate-specific report he cited could not be read, so the support rests on industry-wide figures.
limitations: The Stargate-specific costs Marcus pointed to were not directly checked.
The Bernstein figures come through a translated summary, and one dollar figure in it looks mistyped.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: The costs of developing AI data centers, including OpenAI's Stargate, are rising rapidly.

statement.excerpt: And, breaking news, costs are rapidly rising too:
statement.document_title: An entire industry is being propped up by math that is insane.

from_speaker: cost of developing OpenAI's Stargate & other AI data centers
our_interpretation: Plain reading: around June 2026, the cost of building AI data centers (per unit of capacity, or for set projects) was going up fast.
Strong rises over a year or a hardware generation, such as double-digit per-gigawatt increases or multi-fold component price rises, count as 'rapid'.
criteria.support_condition: Credible estimates from early to mid 2026 show AI data center build costs rising sharply, per gigawatt or through key parts such as memory.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Credible estimates from the period show AI data center build costs flat or falling.

evidence.excerpt: the total AI data center capex comes to about $4.73 billion per gigawatt—a 17% increase compared to the roughly $4.05 billion in the previous Blackwell cycle.
evidence.publisher: Bitget News (translating Wallstreetcn, citing Bernstein Research)
evidence.explanation: Bernstein's June 8, 2026 estimate puts the cost of a gigawatt of AI data center capacity 17% above the previous chip generation. That is a sharp rise in build cost at the time of the post. The translated dollar figure appears to be off by a factor of ten, but the percentage rise is stated directly.

evidence.excerpt: NAND prices have risen 11.3 times from April 2023 lows to May 2026, an annualized rate of 115%
evidence.locator: section 'Rack Cost: The Underlying Logic of $9.1 Million', paragraph 3
evidence.publisher: Bitget News (translating Wallstreetcn, citing Bernstein Research)
evidence.explanation: Storage, a major part of rack cost, rose in price at about 115% a year through May 2026. Bernstein says memory and storage are the main reason rack costs exceeded earlier estimates.

evidence.excerpt: The Malaysian market recorded a 9.3% year-on-year increase in construction costs as artificial intelligence (AI) accelerates and reshapes how facilities are designed, powered, and built.
evidence.explanation: Shows AI-driven construction cost inflation in another region during the period. It covers building costs only, not chips.

evidence.excerpt: Average server prices more than doubled between late 2023 and late 2025, according to Bloomberg Intelligence, and prices for the memory used in data centers have risen more than fivefold in a year.
evidence.locator: section 'Why are they so expensive?', paragraph 2
evidence.explanation: Shows the broader trend of fast-rising equipment costs. The dates only partly overlap the claim period, so it is context only.
